Let T retrain T_{\mathrm{retrain}} denote the minimal number of training steps required to retrain a model from scratch on the retain set D r D_{r} so as to achieve the same performance guarantee as that certified for NFT after T T unlearning steps. By construction, any procedure that attains this guarantee in fewer than T retrain T_{\mathrm{retrain}} steps would constitute a faster retraining algorithm, contradicting the definition of T retrain T_{\mathrm{retrain}} . In the standard NFT analysis, the number of unlearning steps T T is fixed in advance as a function of the privacy budget ( ε , δ ) (\varepsilon,\delta) , the learning rate, and the clipping parameters. Crucially, T T does not depend on the initialization of the model parameters. Moreover, the certified guarantee is formulated in the worst case: it requires NFT to produce indistinguishable outcomes for any two initializations. Suppose that NFT, when initialized at the fully trained model x ^ \hat{\textbf{x}} , reaches performance at least α \alpha with probability p p after T T steps, where T ≪ T retrain T\ll T_{\mathrm{retrain}} . Since the guarantee is initialization-agnostic and holds for any model, we may instead initialize NFT from a randomly initialized model 𝐱 init \mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{init}} .
